forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred over the Bight will slowly move east into the Tasman Sea by late Saturday. A cold front is forecast to move across the Bight on Saturday before moving across the southeast of SA on Sunday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible morning fog and frost on and east of the ranges. Chance of isolated light showers about the southern agricultural area. Maximum temperatures below average. Variable winds across the south, tending northeast to southeasterly winds in the north.

Possible morning fog and frost about the agricultural area. Frost also possible about the North West Pastoral district. Maximum temperatures average to below average. Variable winds across the southeast, tending northeast to southeasterly elsewhere.
Dry, with morning frost about the northern agricultural area and pastoral districts. Maximum temperatures below average. North to northeasterly winds.

text.p: Morning frost about the northern agricultural area and pastoral districts. Isolated showers developing about the coast during the morning, extending across the agricultural areas during the afternoon. Maximum temperatures near average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, with a southwesterly change moving across the west during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Sunday: Less than 1 mm about the northern agricultural area with falls between 1 to 5 mm about the southern agricultural area. Isolated falls of 5 to 10 mm possible about the Mt Lofty Ranges.
